paragraphs: Here's what I see in this passage, friend: the church is growing, and growing means problems, like widows being overlooked in the daily food distribution (Acts 6:1). The Twelve don't ignore it and they don't take it all on themselves. They say it's "unacceptable for us to neglect the word of God in order to wait on tables," so the church picks seven men to handle the job (Acts 6:2-3). Nobody's job there is small, because serving widows and teaching the word both matter, and each one gets people devoted to it.

Notice who gets chosen. They're men "confirmed to be full of the Spirit and wisdom," and Stephen is described as "a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit" (Acts 6:3, 5). Then the spotlight turns to Stephen, who is "full of grace and power" and performing "great wonders and signs among the people" (Acts 6:8). And the apostles didn't just hand out tasks, they prayed and laid their hands on the seven (Acts 6:6).

Then the pushback comes, with false witnesses and a mob, and Stephen gets seized (Acts 6:11-13). But look at the last line: they "saw that his face was like the face of an angel" (Acts 6:15). Being full of the Spirit doesn't mean nobody will fight you. Keep serving and keep your eyes on the word, baker, because Stephen's story is NOT over.
